data.name: Wuxing Master 五行师(CCG)
data.detailed_description:
"Wuxing Master 五行师(CCG)" is a Collectible Card Game(CCG) whose rules and numerical value have been honed for ten years. Both the appearance and content are pursuing a strong Chinese style.
Compared with other CCG, there are some unique rules: You have to sacrifice a card from your hand if you want to raise your upper limit of mana, there are six attack routes on a battlefield and any cards can be matched without the restrictions of professions.
The rules and numerical value of "Wuxing Master 五行师(CCG)" originated from an independent game which was launched ten years ago. This independent game have gained many fans based on its playability even without promotion funds, and its combat rules and numerical value have become mature and balanced after a lot of people’s long -term playing. Now "Wuxing Master 五行师(CCG)" is striving to become a high-quality product of CCG after two years’ efforts.

reviews.review:
This is a really good game that is actually not at all like Hearthstone. If I had to compare it to any game, it would be the excellent but sadly discontinued Might and Magic: Duel of Champions.

There are three types of cards: Creature cards, Spell cards and Equipment cards.
These are tied to one of five different colours corresponding to the Chinese elements: Wood, Water, Metal, Fire and Earth.
Decks have a minimum of 40 cards, can include a maximum of 3 of the same card, and can be a single colour or a combination of any of the five colours.

Here's the, very clever, catch. Like Hearthstone, you also have a 'Leader ability' which you can select when building your deck. However, your leader ability will be much worse the more different colours your deck includes.
Single colour decks tend to have beneficial reusable abilities, dual colour decks tend to have single use abilities while decks with three colours or more will generally only have disadvantages to choose from such as being able to play only one card a turn, damaging one of your units by 1 at the start of each turn or only being able to play 1 of each card in your deck rather than the usual 3.

The cards themselves are cleverly designed as well. Cards automatically attack the spot opposing them, or the enemy leader if the spot opposing them is empty. This may seem like it limits design space but in fact it opens up room for a LOT of positioning related abilities and also allows many creatures to have activated abilities. The abilities are extremely diverse. Some, like Charge, will be familiar to those who have played games Hearthstone while others will be completely different. There is for example an ability which allows a creature attacking an enemy creature to deal extra damage to the opponent depending on how much its attack is higher than the opposing creatures attack (sort of like an attack-based MtG Trample ability). Unfortunately many of these abilities are fairly hard to translate and explain as the game is off course, entirely in Chinese.

The game is generous in terms of what free cards it gives you as well. You can get free stuff both through story mode duels as well as puzzles and there is a large number of quests and achievements. It is entirely possible to play it entirely F2P although buying cards is really cheap in comparison to western CCGs as well due to the Chinese pricing. Add to that a large number of game modes: Practice, Ranked, Puzzles, Arena and Tournaments to name a few and this game is well, well worth a recommendation.
